subject: knight
reasoning:
I'm thinking through how to build an armored knight model using the SDK, trying to stick to conservative, documented API calls like joints and chains since I can't verify unfamiliar methods by testing.

Since exact signatures for capsules and rods are uncertain, I'm leaning toward a safer approach: creating joints via b.joint and then attaching plain THREE.js meshes as children, positioning them relative to each joint's world location with shared cached materials for efficiency.

I'm sketching out the knight's skeleton proportions — hips, spine, chest, neck, head, jaw, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, ankles — along with a loose A-pose stance, plans for a helmet with a chin guard, and a sword and shield gripped in the hands. I'm also working out a helper function to build limb segments as cylinders oriented between two joint points using quaternion alignment.

Now I'm writing out the actual body parts: a tasseted pelvis skirt with a gold belt buckle, a tapered chest cylinder with a breastplate ridge and gorget, and rounded pauldrons with gold trim at the shoulders.

Continuing to shapes...

Checking blade positioning so it doesn't clip through the forearm—I'll offset the sword forward in z to avoid overlap, keeping the grip near the wrist with the blade angled up and slightly forward.

I'm placing the shield on the left forearm as a kite-shaped extruded mesh with a gold boss and cross emblem, then setting up the color palette and material caching before building out the joint hierarchy starting from the hips.
